assessments.reasoning: The Computer History Museum's Software Preservation archive serves the original report scan. Its dated cover identifies the report number, authors, and Digital SRC, and its copyright page identifies Olivetti. The captured complete source exactly matches the registered digest d022f91be1a904dd1ed3ea76a04744eec89ff4e278fc0588f279c9b39714f73a. The identified controlling passage is §4 Declarations, Opaque types and Revelations, printed page 31 / PDF page 43. The November 1989 Modula-3 report describes an opaque type as naming an unspecified reference subtype. A definitive revelation makes the concrete type known in its scope, while a partial revelation gives a subtype constraint. The full branding and well-formedness restrictions remain part of the source. The 1990 amendment is outside this statement. The base text explicitly allows several partial revelations but exactly one definitive revelation, and makes revelation scope material.
